briefing.opening: Good day. Welcome to today's Climate Change Daily Briefing for November 21, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 COP31 Enters Overtime: Severe Deadlock Over Fossil Fuel Phaseout
sections.content: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP31), held in Antalya, Türkiye, has officially entered overtime after failing to reach a consensus following the exclusion of fossil fuel language from the draft agreement [19, 27, 29, 35]. With nearly 200 nations participating, the EU climate chief warned that 'no deal is better than a bad deal,' mounting a final push backed by 130 countries to include language on the phaseout of oil, gas, and coal [20, 27, 40, 41]. However, conflicts with oil-producing nations, disinformation, and sharp disagreements over lukewarm commitments have sparked mounting warnings that the summit risks collapsing and becoming one of the most disappointing in history [24, 25, 26, 30].

sections.title: ⚠️ Accelerating Extreme Weather and Warnings of Ecological and Human Rights Disasters
sections.content: Amid deepening climate change that has made the likelihood of supercharged hurricanes 23 times higher, concerns have been raised that declining atmospheric dust concentrations could further accelerate global warming [1, 34]. On-the-ground damage is also becoming starkly visible: at Dade Correctional Institution in Florida, an inmate died from respiratory distress amid extreme heat reaching 119°F, while in the Bering Sea, following the die-off of 10 billion snow crabs due to marine heatwaves, an unprecedented hybrid crab species has emerged, disrupting marine ecosystems [42, 43]. Amid such worsening climate disasters, food and nutrition policies for vulnerable children remain sidelined, while psychological trauma and mental health issues caused by these disasters are increasingly highlighted as critical challenges [3, 31].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Power Infrastructure and Renewable Energy Transition to Secure Domestic Industrial Competitiveness
sections.content: As the geopolitical landscape shifts from the era of oil to one of minerals, electricity, and carbon, President Lee has officially called for securing national industrial competitiveness through renewable energy to keep pace with surging demand for AI and memory semiconductors [2, 16]. In line with this, the International Energy Agency (IEA) presented concrete solutions, emphasizing that the buildout of transmission grids and energy storage systems (ESS) is essential for South Korea's successful renewable energy expansion [18]. In the power sector, Korea Western Power has moved to secure practical execution capabilities by appointing 20 specialists and expanding its advisory framework to bolster expertise in renewable energy project development [13, 15].

sections.title: 🌱 Technological Innovation and the Spread of Community-Driven Carbon Neutrality Initiatives
sections.content: As the IPCC and the IEA reaffirmed the critical necessity of CCUS technologies to achieve 1.5°C net-zero goals, global energy transition efforts continue, with Spain bolstering support for aging wind farm repowering and storage facilities, and India signing a 300MW solar-and-battery supply agreement [14, 17, 33]. At the local and municipal levels in South Korea, plans are underway to revamp aging ports into 'renewable energy hubs,' while everyday community-oriented policies are taking root, such as 29 localities across Gyeonggi Province converting carbon neutrality points into local currency [10, 12]. Furthermore, grassroots carbon neutrality capabilities are yielding tangible results, including Yeongdo District's carbon-neutral village 'Tantan Daero 1.5' receiving the Minister of Environment Award, and Sun Moon University hosting a graduation ceremony for energy transition workforce training [4, 6].

briefing.closing: Even amid fierce international conflicts over greenhouse gas emissions reductions, actionable measures for the energy transition and climate adaptation must be accelerated across all sectors. That concludes today's climate briefing.
